property_summary: For any bytes4 interfaceId, calling supportsInterface(interfaceId) on the contract always returns true for the IAccessControl interface ID.
Calling supportsInterface with the IAccessControl interface ID always returns true after a cancel operation.
After any operation, calling supportsInterface(type(IAccessControl).interfaceId) returns true if the operation does not revert.
After any call to cancel(bytes32) that reverts or succeeds, the contract's supportsInterface returns true for IAccessControl interface ID.
The contract always returns true for supportsInterface(type(IAccessControl).interfaceId) after any public call to cancel.
For any id, if cancel(id) succeeds, then after the call hasRole(PROPOSER_ROLE, address(this)) must be true.
If cancel(id) succeeds, then the caller must have the PROPOSER_ROLE before the call.
After a successful cancel, the operation cannot be pending.
Before cancel(id) reverts, the caller must have the PROPOSER_ROLE if PROPOSER_ROLE admin is not address(0).
If cancel(id) succeeds, then hasRole(PROPOSER_ROLE, address(this)) must be true before the call.
cancel() should revert when the caller is not a proposer and the operation is pending
cancel can only be called by an account with PROPOSER_ROLE.
hasRole returns true for any role and account, so cancel should always revert when called from a non-proposer account.
Only accounts with PROPOSER_ROLE can cancel pending operations.
When hasRole always returns true, cancel can be called by any account without reverting, violating the proposer-only restriction.
After scheduling an operation, cancelling it must make the operation not pending.
After an operation is cancelled, calling cancel again with the same id should revert.
When an operation is cancelled, the caller must have the PROPOSER_ROLE.
Calling cancel on an operation that is pending always reverts if the caller does not have the PROPOSER_ROLE.
If an account has the PROPOSER_ROLE, then cancel should succeed and make the operation not pending.
After cancel() is called, the operation's timestamp should be deleted (zero) regardless of the caller's role.
After cancel() is called, if the caller has the PROPOSER_ROLE, the operation's pending status should be false (i.e., getTimestamp(id) == 0).
After calling cancel, isOperationPending(id) returns false for the cancelled id.
After a PROPOSER_ROLE holder cancels an operation, the operation's timestamp is reset to 0.
After cancel() is called for an operation, the operation's timestamp remains unchanged (not zeroed) only if the caller does not have PROPOSER_ROLE.

For any id, after scheduling it and waiting the delay, cancel must revert because the operation is pending; the bug makes cancel always succeed, violating the invariant that cancellation of non-existent operations reverts.
For any operation ID that has been scheduled and then executed, calling cancel must revert.
For any operation that is not scheduled (never had its timestamp set), isOperation returns false, so cancel must revert because the operation is not pending.
For any operation id, if isOperation returns false, then cancel must revert.
If isOperation returns false, then cancel must revert.
A set of two equal operations (same target,value,data,predecessor,salt) scheduled with delay 0 is ready or pending after the second schedule returns; cancel reverts when the operation is not pending.
For any operation id, if isOperation returns true then cancel should not revert.
If isOperation(id) returns true, then cancel(id) should not revert.
For any operation id, cancel(id) reverts if and only if isOperation(id) returns false (i.e., getTimestamp(id) == 0).
For any operation id with block timestamp less than the scheduled timestamp, cancel(id) should revert.
For any id, if cancel() is called and does not revert, then after the call isOperation(id) must return false (i.e., the operation is no longer pending).
After a successful cancel(id), getTimestamp(id) must be 0, not 1.
After a successful cancel(id), isOperation(id) must return false (i.e., the timestamp is not > 0).
For any id, if isOperation(id) returns true, then getTimestamp(id) must be strictly greater than 0 (not just non-zero).
For any id, if cancel(id) does not revert, then before the cancel call, isOperation(id) must return true exactly when getTimestamp(id) > 0 (not just != 0).
Cancelling a pending operation whose timestamp is > _DONE_TIMESTAMP should succeed, but the bug always reverts because isOperation returns false.
The contract's `isOperation` function should return true for any operation that has a timestamp greater than 0.
For any bytes32 id, if c.isOperation(id) returns true, then c.isOperationPending(id) must return true.
For any bytes32 id, if c.getTimestamp(id) > 0, then c.isOperation(id) must return true.
For any operation id, if getTimestamp returns a value greater than 0, then isOperation must return true.
For any operation id, if cancel(id) succeeds then isOperationPending(id) must become false (i.e., revert when trying to cancel again).
isOperationPending returns true only for timestamps greater than _DONE_TIMESTAMP, so cancel should only succeed when isOperationPending is true.
After a successful cancel, isOperationPending returns false for the same operation id.
If isOperationPending returns false for an id, then cancel(id) must revert.
For any operation id, cancel(id) should not revert if and only if isOperationPending(id) returns true before the call.
For any operation id, if isOperationPending returns true, then getTimestamp must be strictly greater than _DONE_TIMESTAMP (i.e., pending implies not exactly at _DONE_TIMESTAMP).
Cancelling a pending operation leaves the operation not pending.
If an operation is pending, then its timestamp is strictly greater than _DONE_TIMESTAMP (i.e., a pending operation cannot have timestamp exactly equal to _DONE_TIMESTAMP).

After cancelling a scheduled non-duplicate operation, its timestamp becomes 0 (not pending), and the rule is that for any operation, if getTimestamp returns exactly _DONE_TIMESTAMP (1), then isOperationPending returns true, which holds in the reference but fails in the mutant because the mutant's isOperationPending returns true also for timestamp = _DONE_TIMESTAMP, but after cancel the timestamp is 0, so this rule is about the invariant that a timestamp of 1 always implies pending.
If an operation's timestamp is exactly _DONE_TIMESTAMP (1), then isOperationPending must return true
After a successful cancel, the operation's timestamp should be 0 so it is not pending.
After cancel, isOperationPending returns false for that operation id.
The return value of isOperationPending(id) after a successful cancel(id) is consistently false.
A cancelled operation's id should not be pending, but the bug makes it pending.
After canceling an operation, its timestamp is 0, making isOperationPending return false.
An operation that is pending exactly at the current block timestamp is ready (can be executed) in the reference.
If an operation is not pending, it should also not be ready.
If isOperationPending returns true and isOperationDone returns false, then isOperationReady should return true when block.timestamp equals the operation's timestamp.
If isOperationReady once returns true for an operation id, then before any other transaction that id should remain ready (or become done) but not become unready.
An operation scheduled with a zero delay is immediately ready in the reference but not in the mutant.
After a cancel, the operation id is no longer pending, meaning isOperationPending returns false.
After a successful cancel, the operation id is not done, meaning isOperationDone returns false.
Calling cancel on a pending operation id always leaves the operation id not pending (isOperationPending returns false) immediately after the cancel.
After canceling a pending operation, isOperationDone always returns false for that operation id.
After canceling a scheduled operation that is not yet ready, the operation id should be neither pending nor done.
After cancelling an operation, isOperationDone returns true for the cancelled id.
After canceling an operation, isOperationDone returns false for that operation's id.
isOperationDone returns false for any operation that has been cancelled.
If an operation is pending (not done), then isOperationDone returns false for its id.
For any operation id, isOperationDone always returns true after cancel() reverts with 'TimelockController: operation cannot be cancelled'
After any cancel call, the canceled operation id should be done (isOperationDone returns true).
isOperationDone returns true if and only if the operation timestamp equals _DONE_TIMESTAMP
After canceling a pending operation, the operation should be done (isOperationDone returns true).
After any cancel call, the operation's isOperationDone should return true.
After canceling an operation with a given id, isOperationDone for that id always returns true if the operation was pending.
After scheduling an operation, calling cancel on it should correctly indicate the operation is no longer pending by returning false from isOperationPending.
After canceling a scheduled operation, the operation's timestamp should be 0, as returned by getTimestamp.
After canceling a scheduled operation, the operation's timestamp should be 0, as returned by getTimestamp.
After scheduling an operation and before it is ready, cancel always reverts.
After canceling a scheduled operation, the operation's timestamp should be 0.
